claims.text: Hanja is classified as an extinct language because it is not understood by modern Korean or Chinese speakers, and it was primarily used in historical records before the 20th century.

Hanja, while a writing system based on Chinese characters, has evolved to have unique characteristics that differ significantly from modern Korean and Chinese, further supporting its classification as a dead language.
The lack of research and language models for Hanja indicates its status as a dead language, as it is necessary for exploring Korean history but not actively used in contemporary communication.
